Key audit matter:
Information technology (IT) systems and controls
The Group implemented SAP, a fully integrated financial accounting
and reporting system, effective 1 January 2016 and has continued
to add modules to enhance the system.
Information systems are key to the Group. Any errors, mistakes,
incorrect access rights and omissions from the systems can have a
significant impact on the financial statements. Further, the design
and operating effectiveness of the controls incorporated in SAP is
important to ensure the reliability of the information produced by the
system.
There is a risk that automated accounting procedures and IT
dependent controls on key business processes are not operating
effectively.
How our audit addressed the matter:
We examined the framework of governance over the Group’s IT organisation and
the controls over program development and changes, access to programs and data
and IT operations, including compensating controls where required
We tested the Information Technology General Controls (ITGCs) that ensure
accuracy, completeness and validity of data processing. This entailed the review
of access controls to information and the underlying system and plans put in
place by management to ensure consistent and continuous production of reliable
information.
We tested relevant application controls within the IT system that management relies
on to run the business effectively.
We re-performed selected automated computations and compared our results
with those from the system and the general ledger. Further, we reviewed key
reconciliations between the sub-ledgers and the general ledger.
We tested significant manual journals processed into the system during the period.
